title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages). M is a rank-4 Azumaya algebra over a base S, i.e. a twisted form of M_2(O_S), corresponding to a projective line bundle P over S. σ and ρ are sections of M satisfying σ² = −1 (so Tr σ = 0, det σ = 1) and ρ² = ρ − 1 (so Tr ρ = 1, det ρ = 1). These are the twisted analogues of the order-4 and order-6 generators of SL_2(Z). Both are assumed 'regular', meaning scalar on no fibre. Grothendieck wants to show that N := ρ + σ is idempotent: (75) N² − N = 0.

Strategy. By Cayley–Hamilton, N² − (Tr N)N + det N = 0. So for N regular, (75) is equivalent to (77): Tr N = 1 and det N = 0. The previous page shows, via a fibrewise argument ending in the contradiction ρ = 0, that N is never scalar on a fibre. Hence this page opens 'Donc N est régulier, il reste à prouver (77)'.

Trace. Tr N = Tr σ + Tr ρ = 0 + 1 = 1.

Determinant. A first attempt, det(ρ+σ) = det ρ + det σ + Tr(σρ), is crossed out; its sign is wrong. He then factors:
- det(σ+ρ) = det σ · det(1 + σ⁻¹ρ).
- For 2×2 matrices, det(1+X) = 1 + Tr X + det X.
- Here σ⁻¹ = −σ, so X = σ⁻¹ρ = −σρ, Tr X = −Tr(σρ), and det X = (det σ)⁻¹ det ρ = 1.
- Therefore det(σ+ρ) = 2 − Tr(σρ).

Conclusion. det N = 0 is equivalent to Tr(σρ) = 2, labelled (69). Since det(σρ) = 1, this says σρ is fibrewise unipotent, i.e. σρ = 1 + N₀ with N₀ nilpotent, matching ε₀ = 1 + N₀ on the previous page. In SL_2(Z) the product of the order-4 and order-6 generators is indeed a unipotent translation.

The page ends with a note to self: for the proofs (in the remaining cases) one can proceed 'as before', starting from (68) instead of (75); 'not entirely elucidated — come back to it!'. The next page begins a fresh recapitulation ('VII Récapitulation sur les épi-glabres') on regular sections of forms of GL(2), SL(2), PGL(2).
errors: The crossed-out formula det(ρ+σ) = det ρ + det σ + Tr(σρ) is wrong. The correct identity is det(A+B) = det A + det B + Tr A·Tr B − Tr(AB), which here gives 2 − Tr(σρ). Grothendieck abandoned it and redid the computation correctly via det σ·det(1+σ⁻¹ρ).
The final computation is correct. The page explicitly marks the overall argument (the equivalence of (68), (69) and (75) in all cases) as not fully elucidated.

ideas.what: For a regular (fibrewise non-scalar) section N of a rank-4 Azumaya algebra, N is idempotent iff Tr N = 1 and det N = 0 (Cayley–Hamilton).
ideas.modern_name: Cayley–Hamilton characterisation of rank-one idempotents in M_2

ideas.what: det(σ+ρ) = 2 − Tr(σρ) when σ² = −1 and ρ² = ρ − 1; so σ+ρ is an idempotent iff σρ is unipotent (trace 2).
ideas.modern_name: 2×2 determinant identity det(A+B) = det A + det B + TrA·TrB − Tr(AB); unipotent product of the order-4 and order-6 generators of SL_2(Z)

ideas.what: Twisted (Azumaya / Brauer–Severi) versions of the SL_2(Z) generator relations, used as data ('épi-glabres') in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'.
ideas.modern_name: forms of GL_2 / PGL_2 with order-4 and order-6 sections; relations of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 in a twisted setting
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to themes of La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Routine 2×2 linear-algebra verification inside a larger unpublished project on twisted SL_2(Z)-type relations. The page itself contains no new result beyond a correct trace and determinant computation and a note to revisit the argument.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Donc N est régulier, il reste à prouver (77).' — not 'N inv[?] singulier'.
'(cas des moins testés)' is uncertain; it is an inserted parenthetical whose reading is doubtful.
'exprimant je puis partir de (68)' is likely 'excepté que je puis partir de (68), au lieu de (75)'.
The left-margin note reads roughly 'calculs déjà faits ? i.e. ? Voir (cf formule (69))'.
